metadata.title: Empirical Margin Distributions and Bounding the Generalization Error of Combined Classifiers
metadata.source_note: Extracted from PDF→text fallback; .tex source not available. Math fidelity reduced.

nodes.name: Generalization error of a classifier
nodes.statement: For predictor $\mathrm{sign}(g(X))$ of label $Y \in \{-1,1\}$, the generalization (classification) error is $P\{Y g(X) \le 0\}$.
nodes.statement_clean: Probability that the predictor disagrees with the label.

nodes.name: Margin of a classifier
nodes.statement: The margin of a classifier $\hat g$ on labeled example $(X,Y)$ is the product $Y\hat g(X)$.

nodes.name: Gaussian complexity function
nodes.statement: $G_n(\mathcal{F}) := \mathbb{E}\,\|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n g_i \delta_{X_i}\|_{\mathcal{F}}$ where $\{g_i\}$ are i.i.d. standard normal independent of $\{X_i\}$.

nodes.name: Rademacher complexity function
nodes.statement: $R_n(\mathcal{F}) := \mathbb{E}\,\|n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n \varepsilon_i \delta_{X_i}\|_{\mathcal{F}}$ where $\{\varepsilon_i\}$ are i.i.d. Rademacher (\pm 1 with probability 1/2) independent of $\{X_i\}$.

nodes.name: Margin cost function family
nodes.statement: A countable family $\Phi = \{\varphi_k : k \ge 1\}$ of Lipschitz functions $\varphi_k : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ such that $I_{(-\infty,0]}(x) \le \varphi_k(x)$ for all $k$; $L(\varphi)$ denotes the Lipschitz constant.

nodes.name: Random $\varepsilon$-entropy
nodes.statement: Given metric space $(T,d)$, $H_d(T;\varepsilon) := \log N_d(T;\varepsilon)$ where $N_d(T;\varepsilon)$ is the minimal number of $\varepsilon$-radius balls covering $T$. Used with metric $d_{P_n,2}(f,g) := (P_n |f-g|^2)^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: $\gamma$-margin and empirical $\gamma$-margin
nodes.statement: For $\gamma \in (0,1]$: $\delta_n(\gamma;f) := \sup\{\delta \in (0,1) : \delta^\gamma P\{f \le \delta\} \le n^{-1+\gamma/2}\}$ and $\hat\delta_n(\gamma;f) := \sup\{\delta \in (0,1) : \delta^\gamma P_n\{f \le \delta\} \le n^{-1+\gamma/2}\}$.

nodes.name: $\gamma$-bound
nodes.statement: The quantity $1/(n^{1-\gamma/2}\hat\delta_n(\gamma;g)^\gamma)$ is called the $\gamma$-bound of classifier $g$; it decreases as $\gamma$ decreases from 1 to 0.

nodes.name: Lévy distance
nodes.statement: $L(F,G) := \inf\{\delta > 0 : F(t) \le G(t+\delta)+\delta \text{ and } G(t) \le F(t+\delta)+\delta, \forall t \in \mathbb{R}\}$.

nodes.name: Glivenko–Cantelli class $GC(P)$
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F} \in GC(P)$ iff $\|P_n - P\|_{\mathcal{F}} \to 0$ a.s. as $n \to \infty$. Bounded CLT class $BCLT(P)$: $\mathbb{E}\|P_n-P\|_{\mathcal{F}} = O(n^{-1/2})$.

nodes.name: Multiclass margin
nodes.statement: For $f$ predicting label $y \in \mathcal{Y}$ for $x$, the margin is $m_f(x,y) := f(x,y) - \max_{y' \ne y} f(x,y')$; misclassification iff $m_f(x,y) \le 0$.

nodes.name: Closed convex hull $\mathrm{conv}(H)$
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{conv}(H)$ consists of pointwise limits of convex combinations $\sum_{j=1}^N w_j^N h_j^N$ with $w_j^N \ge 0$, $\sum_j w_j^N = 1$, $h_j^N \in H$.

nodes.name: Feedforward neural network class $\mathcal{N}_l$ and $\mathcal{H}_l$
nodes.statement: Networks with base class $H$, $l$ layers of neurons, and sigmoids $\{\sigma_j\}$ with Lipschitz constants $\{L_j\}$. Layer-$j$ neuron computes $N_{\sigma_j,w}(u_1,\dots,u_n) = \sigma_j(\sum_i w_i u_i)$.

nodes.name: Weight-restricted networks $\mathcal{H}_j(A_1,\dots,A_j)$
nodes.statement: Recursive class of networks where each layer-$j$ neuron has weight vector $w$ with $\|w\|_1 \le A_j$.

nodes.name: Network complexity functionals $G(f)$ and $H_\alpha(f)$
nodes.statement: $G(f) := \prod_{k=1}^{\ell(f)}(4 L_k W_k(f) + 1)$ and $H_\alpha(f) := \sum_{k=1}^{\ell(f)} \sqrt{(\alpha/2)\log(2 + |\log_2 W_k(f)|)}$ where $W_k(f) := \max_N \|w^{(N)}\|_1 \vee b_k$.

nodes.name: Penalized estimator $\tilde f_S$
nodes.statement: $\tilde f_S := \arg\min_{f \in F}\{P_n\{\tilde f \le 0\} + \inf_{\delta \in (0,1]} \hat\pi_n(f;\delta)\}$ where $\hat\pi_n(f;\delta) := P_n\{0 < \tilde f \le \delta\} + J_n(f;\delta)$ and $J_n(f;\delta) := (2\sqrt{2\pi}/\delta) G(f) G_n(H) + ((\log\log_2(2\delta^{-1}))/n)^{1/2} + H_\alpha(f)/\sqrt{n}$.

nodes.name: Theorem 1 (margin–cost generalization bounds)
nodes.statement: For all $t > 0$, $P\{\exists f \in \mathcal{F} : P\{f \le 0\} > \inf_{k \ge 1}[P_n \varphi_k(f) + 4 L(\varphi_k) R_n(\mathcal{F}) + ((\log k)/n)^{1/2}] + t/\sqrt{n}\} \le 2 \exp(-2t^2)$, with an analogous Gaussian-complexity version.
assumptions: $\mathcal{F}$ is a class of measurable functions, $\{f(x) : f \in \mathcal{F}\}$ bounded for all $x$
conclusions: $P\{\exists f \in \mathcal{F} : P\{f \le 0\} > \inf_k [P_n\varphi_k(f) + 4L(\varphi_k)R_n(\mathcal{F}) + ((\log k)/n)^{1/2}] + t/\sqrt{n}\} \le 2 e^{-2t^2}$

nodes.name: Theorem 2 (margin bound, special $\Phi_0$ family)
nodes.statement: For all $t > 0$, $P\{\exists f \in \mathcal{F} : P\{f \le 0\} > \inf_{\delta \in (0,1]}[P_n \varphi(f/\delta) + 8L(\varphi)R_n(\mathcal{F})/\delta + ((\log\log_2(2\delta^{-1}))/n)^{1/2}] + t/\sqrt{n}\} \le 2 \exp(-2t^2)$.
conclusions: Margin-type generalization bound parameterized by $\delta$

nodes.name: Theorem 3 (lower margin bound)
nodes.statement: For all $t > 0$, $P\{\exists f \in \mathcal{F} : P\{f \le 0\} < \sup_{\delta \in (0,1]}[P_n \varphi(f/\delta) - 8L(\varphi)R_n(\mathcal{F})/\delta - ((\log\log_2(2\delta^{-1}))/n)^{1/2}] - t/\sqrt{n}\} \le 2 \exp(-2t^2)$.
conclusions: Lower-side counterpart of Theorem 2

nodes.name: Theorem 4 (uniform deviation bounds in terms of margin gap)
nodes.statement: For all $t > 0$, $P\{\exists f \in \mathcal{F} : P_n\{f \le 0\} - P\{f \le 0\} > \inf_{\delta \in (0,1]}[P_n\{|f| \le \delta\} + \Delta_n(\mathcal{F};\delta)] + t/\sqrt{n}\} \le 4\exp(-2t^2)$, with $\Delta_n(\mathcal{F};\delta) := 8R_n(\mathcal{F})/\delta + ((\log\log_2(2\delta^{-1}))/n)^{1/2}$, plus the analogous bound replacing $P_n$ with $P$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{F}$ measurable function class as in Section 2
conclusions: Uniform two-sided concentration of empirical and true error in terms of small-margin mass

nodes.name: Theorem 5 ($\gamma$-margin equivalence under entropy growth)
nodes.statement: If $H_{d_{P_n,2}}(\mathcal{F};u) \le D u^{-\alpha}$ a.s. for some $\alpha \in (0,2)$, $D > 0$, then for any $\gamma \ge 2\alpha/(2+\alpha)$ and constants $A,B > 0$: $P\{\forall f \in \mathcal{F} : A^{-1}\hat\delta_n(\gamma;f) \le \delta_n(\gamma;f) \le A \hat\delta_n(\gamma;f)\} \ge 1 - B \log_2\log_2 n \exp(-n^{\gamma/2}/2)$.
conclusions: Empirical and true $\gamma$-margins are within multiplicative constant $A$ with high probability
Implies $P\{f \le 0\} \le \mathrm{const}/(n^{1-\gamma/2}\hat\delta_n(\gamma;f)^\gamma)$

nodes.name: Theorem 6 (concentration on small-mass sublevel sets)
nodes.statement: Under the entropy condition $H_{d_{P_n,2}}(\mathcal{F};u) \le D u^{-\alpha}$, for $\varepsilon \ge (1/(n\delta^\alpha))^{2/(2+\alpha)} \vee (2\log n)/n$ and large $n$: $P\{\exists f \in \mathcal{F} : P_n\{f \le \delta\} \le \varepsilon \text{ and } P\{f \le \delta/2\} \ge A\varepsilon\} \le B\log_2\log_2 \varepsilon^{-1} \exp(-n\varepsilon/2)$, plus the symmetric version exchanging $P$ and $P_n$.
conclusions: Two-sided concentration linking $P_n\{f\le\delta\}$ and $P\{f\le\delta/2\}$

nodes.name: Theorem 7 (uniform Lévy convergence iff truncated GC)
nodes.statement: Assume $\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} P\{|f| \ge M\} \to 0$ as $M \to \infty$. Then $\mathcal{F}_M \in GC(P)$ for all $M > 0$ iff $\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} L(F_{n,f}, F_f) \to 0$ a.s.
conclusions: $\mathcal{F}_M \in GC(P)$ for all $M > 0$ iff $\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} L(F_{n,f}, F_f) \to 0$ a.s.

nodes.name: Theorem 8 (GC characterization via Lévy convergence + envelope)
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F} \in GC(P)$ iff there exists a $P$-integrable envelope for $\mathcal{F}^{(c)} = \{f - Pf : f \in \mathcal{F}\}$ and $\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} L(F_{n,f}, F_f) \to 0$ a.s.
conclusions: Characterization of $GC(P)$ in terms of integrable envelope and uniform Lévy convergence

nodes.name: Theorem 9 (rates of Lévy convergence)
nodes.statement: If $\mathcal{F}$ is uniformly bounded and $\mathcal{F} \in BCLT(P)$, then $\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} L(F_{n,f}, F_f) = O_P(n^{-1/4})$. If furthermore $H_{d_{P_n,2}}(\mathcal{F};u) \le Du^{-\alpha}$ a.s. for $\alpha \in (0,2)$, then $\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} L(F_{n,f}, F_f) = O(n^{-1/(2+\alpha)})$ a.s.
assumptions: $\mathcal{F} \in BCLT(P)$ for first part; entropy bound $Du^{-\alpha}$ for second part
conclusions: $\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} L(F_{n,f}, F_f) = O_P(n^{-1/4})$
$\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} L(F_{n,f}, F_f) = O(n^{-1/(2+\alpha)})$ a.s.

nodes.name: Theorem 10 (probabilistic Lévy bound)
nodes.statement: For class $\mathcal{F}$ of measurable functions $S \to [-M,M]$ and all $t > 0$: $P\{\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}} L(F_{n,f}, F_f) \ge 2(\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum \varepsilon_i\delta_{X_i}\|_{\mathcal{F}} + M/\sqrt{n})^{1/2} + t/\sqrt{n}\} \le \exp(-2t^2)$.
conclusions: Uniform-in-$f$ Lévy distance concentration in terms of Rademacher complexity

nodes.name: Theorem 11 (multiclass generalization bound)
nodes.statement: For all $t > 0$: $P\{\exists f \in \tilde{\mathcal{F}} : P\{m_f \le 0\} > \inf_{\delta \in (0,1]}[P_n\{m_f \le \delta\} + 8M(2M-1)R_n(\mathcal{F})/\delta + ((\log\log_2(2\delta^{-1}))/n)^{1/2}] + t/\sqrt{n}\} \le 2 \exp(-2t^2)$.
assumptions: Labels in finite set $\mathcal{Y}$ with $|\mathcal{Y}| = M$
conclusions: Multiclass margin-based generalization bound with factor $M(2M-1)$

nodes.name: Theorem 12 (boosting / convex-combination bound)
nodes.statement: Let $\mathcal{F} := \mathrm{conv}(H)$. For all $t > 0$: $P\{\exists f \in \mathcal{F} : P\{\tilde f \le 0\} > \inf_{\delta \in (0,1]}[P_n \varphi(\tilde f/\delta) + 8L(\varphi)R_n(H)/\delta + ((\log\log_2(2\delta^{-1}))/n)^{1/2}] + t/\sqrt{n}\} \le 2 \exp(-2t^2)$.
conclusions: Improves Schapire et al. (1998) margin bound for boosting on VC base classes

nodes.name: Theorem 13 (neural network bound, fixed weight bounds)
nodes.statement: For all $t > 0, l \ge 1$: $P\{\exists f \in \mathcal{H}_l(A_1,\dots,A_l) : P\{\tilde f \le 0\} > \inf_{\delta\in(0,1]}[P_n\varphi(\tilde f/\delta) + (2\sqrt{2\pi}L(\varphi)/\delta)\prod_{j=1}^l(2 L_j A_j + 1)G_n(H) + (t+2)/\sqrt{n}]\} \le 2\exp(-2t^2)$.
assumptions: $\mathcal{H}_l(A_1,\dots,A_l)$: $l$-layer feedforward networks with $\|w\|_1 \le A_j$ at layer $j$
conclusions: Margin generalization bound with complexity factor $\prod_{j=1}^l (2L_jA_j+1)$ replacing Bartlett's $(AL)^{l(l+1)/2}$

nodes.name: Theorem 14 (neural network bound, adaptive weight scales)
nodes.statement: For all $t > 0$ and $\alpha > 0$ with $\zeta(\alpha) < 3/2$: $P\{\exists f \in \mathcal{H}_\infty : P\{\tilde f \le 0\} > \inf_{\delta\in(0,1)}[P_n\varphi(\tilde f/\delta) + (2\sqrt{2\pi}L(\varphi)/\delta)G(f)G_n(H) + ((\log\log_2(2\delta^{-1}))/n)^{1/2} + (H_\alpha(f)+t+2)/\sqrt{n}]\} \le 2(3-2\zeta(\alpha))^{-1}\exp(-2t^2)$.
assumptions: $f \in \mathcal{H}_\infty$ feedforward network with arbitrary weight magnitudes
conclusions: Bound holds uniformly over all networks via adaptive complexity functional $G(f)$ and penalty $H_\alpha(f)$

nodes.name: Theorem 15 (oracle inequality for penalized neural network estimator)
nodes.statement: For all $t > 0$ and $\alpha > 0$ with $\zeta(\alpha) < 3/2$: (i) $P\{P\{\tilde f_S \le 0\} > \inf_{f \in F}[P_n\{\tilde f \le 0\} + \inf_\delta \hat\pi_n(f;\delta)] + (t+2)/\sqrt{n}\} \le 2(3-2\zeta(\alpha))^{-1}\exp(-2t^2)$, plus (ii) an oracle inequality controlling $P\{\tilde f_S \le 0\} - \inf_{g \in F} P\{\tilde g \le 0\}$ by $\inf_f[P\{\tilde f \le 0\} - \inf_g P\{\tilde g \le 0\} + \inf_\delta \pi_n(f;\delta)] + (2t+4)/\sqrt{n}$, with probability $\ge 1 - 4(3-2\zeta(\alpha))^{-1}\exp(-2t^2)$.
assumptions: $\tilde f_S$ is the penalized empirical minimizer over $F \subset \mathcal{H}_\infty$
conclusions: Upper confidence bound on generalization error of $\tilde f_S$
Oracle inequality showing optimality of penalization scheme

nodes.name: Lemma 1 (recursive inclusion under concentration)
nodes.statement: Let $N \le \log_2\log_2\varepsilon^{-1}$ with $r_N \ge \varepsilon$. Then on event $E_N \cap J$ (where $J = \{\inf_f P_n\{f \le \delta\} \le \varepsilon\}$): (i) $\forall f \in \mathcal{F}, P_n\{f \le \delta\} \le \varepsilon \Rightarrow f \in \mathcal{F}_N$, and (ii) $\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}_k} P_n\{f \le \delta_k\} \le r_k$ for $0 \le k \le N$.
conclusions: Inductive containment property used in proof of Theorem 6

nodes.name: Lemma 2 (Rademacher bound for max class)
nodes.statement: For class $H$ and $H^{(l)} := \{\max(h_1,\dots,h_l) : h_i \in H\}$: $\mathbb{E}\|\sum_{i=1}^n \varepsilon_i \delta_{X_i}\|_{H^{(l)}} \le 2l\,\mathbb{E}\|\sum_{i=1}^n \varepsilon_i \delta_{X_i}\|_H$.
assumptions: $H$ class of functions; $H^{(l)}$ pointwise maxima of $l$ elements of $H$
conclusions: Rademacher process on $H^{(l)}$ controlled by $2l$ times the Rademacher process on $H$

nodes.name: Proposition 1 (sharpness of $1/\delta$ Rademacher factor)
nodes.statement: For canonical-projection class $\mathcal{F} = \{f_k(x) = x_k\}$ on the random sequence $X_n = (\varepsilon_{kn}(2\log(k+1))^{-1/2})_{k\ge 1}$: $P\{\exists f \in \mathcal{F} : P\{f \le 0\} \ge \inf_{\delta\in(0,1]}[P_n\{f \le \delta\} + 8 R_n(\mathcal{F})/\phi(\delta) + t/\sqrt{n}]\} \to 1$ uniformly for $t \le 2^{-1} n^{1/2}\phi((4n)^{-1/2}) - c$.
conclusions: $1/\delta$ factor in Theorem 2's $R_n(\mathcal{F})/\delta$ term cannot be replaced by $1/\phi(\delta)$

nodes.name: Proposition 2 (optimality of Lévy-convergence rates)
nodes.statement: For $\mathcal{F} = \{f_k(x) = x_k\}$ with $X_n = (\varepsilon_{kn}(2\log(k+1))^{-1/2 - \beta})_{k \ge 1}$, $\beta = 1/\alpha - 1/2$, $\alpha \in (0,2]$: any $\delta_n$ with $\sup_f L(F_{n,f}, F_f) = O_P(\delta_n)$ satisfies $\delta_n \ge c n^{-1/(2+\alpha)}$ (for $\alpha = 2$, $\delta_n \ge cn^{-1/4}$). The matching upper bound holds via Theorem 9.
conclusions: Rates $n^{-1/(2+\alpha)}$ and $n^{-1/4}$ in Theorem 9 are optimal

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 1
nodes.statement: WLOG $\varphi$ takes values in $[0,1]$, so $\varphi(x)=1$ for $x \le 0$. Use $P\{f \le 0\} \le P\varphi(f) \le P_n\varphi(f) + \|P_n - P\|_{G_\varphi}$. Apply martingale concentration, symmetrization, and Rademacher comparison inequality (Ledoux–Talagrand Theorem 4.12), then union bound over $k$.

nodes.name: Reduction $P\{f \le 0\} \le P\varphi(f) \le P_n\varphi(f) + \|P_n - P\|_{G_\varphi}$
nodes.statement: For fixed $\varphi$, $P\{f \le 0\} \le P\varphi(f)$ since $\varphi(x) \ge I_{(-\infty,0]}(x)$, then $P\varphi(f) \le P_n\varphi(f) + \|P_n - P\|_{G_\varphi}$ where $G_\varphi := \{\varphi \circ f - 1 : f \in \mathcal{F}\}$.

nodes.name: Martingale concentration for $\|P_n - P\|_{G_\varphi}$
nodes.statement: Exponential inequality for martingale difference sequences (Devroye, Györfi, Lugosi 1996, pp. 135–136) gives $P\{\|P_n-P\|_{G_\varphi} \ge \mathbb{E}\|P_n - P\|_{G_\varphi} + t/\sqrt{n}\} \le \exp(-2t^2)$.

nodes.name: Symmetrization and Rademacher contraction
nodes.statement: $\mathbb{E}\|P_n - P\|_{G_\varphi} \le 2\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum \varepsilon_i\delta_{X_i}\|_{G_\varphi}$ via symmetrization, then Rademacher comparison (Ledoux–Talagrand Theorem 4.12, p. 112) since $(\varphi-1)/L(\varphi)$ is a contraction with $\varphi(0)-1=0$, giving the factor $2L(\varphi)$.

nodes.name: Union bound over $k$
nodes.statement: Apply (2.4) with $\varphi_k$ and $t$ replaced by $t + \sqrt{\log k}$, sum the geometric tail $\sum_k k^{-2}e^{-2t^2} = (\pi^2/6)e^{-2t^2} \le 2 e^{-2t^2}$.

nodes.name: Gaussian-complexity variant via Slepian's Lemma
nodes.statement: For the Gaussian bound, use Gaussian multiplier inequality: $\mathbb{E}\|P_n-P\|_{G_\varphi} \le \sqrt{2\pi}\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum g_i \delta_{X_i}\|_{G_\varphi}$. Compare Gaussian processes $Z_1, Z_2$ via increments inequality, then apply Slepian's Lemma to obtain $\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum g_i\delta_{X_i}\|_{G_\varphi} \le L(\varphi)\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum g_i\delta_{X_i}\|_{\mathcal{F}} + n^{-1/2}\mathbb{E}|g|$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 2
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 1 to $\varphi_k(\cdot) := \varphi(\cdot/\delta_k)$ with $\delta_k = 2^{-k}$. For $\delta \in (\delta_k, \delta_{k-1}]$, we have $1/\delta_k \le 2/\delta$, $P_n\varphi(f/\delta_k) \le P_n\varphi(f/\delta)$, and $\log k = \log\log_2(1/\delta_k) \le \log\log_2(2/\delta)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 6
nodes.statement: Define recursive sequences $r_k = (C\sqrt\varepsilon)^{2(1-2^{-k})}$, $\delta_k = \delta(1 - \sum \gamma_i)$, classes $\mathcal{F}_k$ and cutoffs $\varphi_k, \varphi_k'$. Apply Talagrand's concentration inequalities (1996a,b; Massart 2000) on events $E^{(k)}$. Use induction (Lemma 1) plus subgaussian-process entropy inequality and Lipschitz property of $\varphi_k$ to control $\mathbb{E}\|P_n - P\|_{G_N}$.

nodes.name: Set up recursive classes and cutoffs
nodes.statement: Define $r_0 = 1$, $r_{k+1} = C\sqrt{r_k\varepsilon}\wedge 1$, $\gamma_k = (\varepsilon/r_k)^{1/2}$, $\delta_k = \delta(1 - \gamma_0 - \dots - \gamma_{k-1})$, $\delta_{k,1/2} = (\delta_k+\delta_{k+1})/2$. Recursive subclasses $\mathcal{F}_{k+1} := \{f \in \mathcal{F}_k : P\{f \le \delta_{k,1/2}\} \le r_{k+1}/2\}$ and Lipschitz cutoffs $\varphi_k, \varphi_k'$.

nodes.name: Apply Talagrand concentration
nodes.statement: On events $E^{(k)} := \{\|P_n-P\|_{G_{k-1}} \le K_1 \mathbb{E}\|P_n-P\|_{G_{k-1}} + K_2 \sqrt{r_{k-1}\varepsilon} + K_3 \varepsilon\} \cap (\text{same for } G_k')$, $P((E^{(k)})^c) \le 2 e^{-n\varepsilon/2}$ via Talagrand concentration.

nodes.name: Inductive containment (Lemma 1)
nodes.statement: By induction on $N$ (Lemma 1), on event $E_N \cap J$: $P_n\{f \le \delta\} \le \varepsilon \Rightarrow f \in \mathcal{F}_N$ and $\sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}_k} P_n\{f \le \delta_k\} \le r_k$.

nodes.name: Entropy/contraction bound on $\mathbb{E}\|P_n-P\|_{G_N}$
nodes.statement: Use subgaussian-entropy inequality (van der Vaart–Wellner 1996, Cor. 2.2.8) plus Lipschitz contraction of $\varphi_N$ ($L = (2/\delta)\sqrt{r_N/\varepsilon}$) and entropy bound $D u^{-\alpha}$, to get $\mathbb{E}\|P_n-P\|_{G_N} \le c\sqrt{r_N\varepsilon}$.

nodes.name: Conclude with $N = [\log_2\log_2\varepsilon^{-1}]$
nodes.statement: Choose $N = [\log_2\log_2\varepsilon^{-1}]$ so that $r_{N+1} \le c\varepsilon$. The second inequality of the theorem follows by symmetric argument exchanging $P$ and $P_n$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 5
nodes.statement: Set $\delta_j := 2^{-j\gamma/2}$, $\varepsilon_j := (1/(n\delta_j^{\alpha'}))^{2/(2+\alpha')}$ with $\alpha' = 2\gamma/(2-\gamma) \ge \alpha$. Apply Theorem 6's first inequality and union over $j$. If $A^{-1}\hat\delta_n(\gamma;f) \le \delta_n(\gamma;f)$ fails for some $f$, derive a contradiction with the bound from Theorem 6.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 10
nodes.statement: For $\delta > 0$ and $\varphi$ piecewise linear ($1$ for $x \le 0$, $0$ for $x \ge 1$), bound $F_f(y) - F_{n,f}(y+\delta) \le \|P_n - P\|_{\tilde G_\delta}$ and the symmetric inequality. Apply Theorem 1's argument with class $\tilde G_\delta = \{\varphi((f-y)/\delta) - 1 : f \in \mathcal{F}, y \in [-M,M]\}$ to obtain $\|P_n - P\|_{\tilde G_\delta} \le (4/\delta)\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum\varepsilon_i\delta_{X_i}\|_\mathcal{F} + Mn^{-1/2} + t/\sqrt{n}$. Optimize $\delta$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 7
nodes.statement: For (i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii): symmetrization plus Theorem 10 with $t = \log n$ and Borel–Cantelli. Use truncation argument with $L(F_f, F_{f_M}) \le \sup_f P\{|f| \ge M\}$. For (ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i): standard inequality $\|P_n - P\|_{\mathcal{F}_M} = \sup_{f \in \mathcal{F}_M} |\int t\,d(F_{n,f} - F_f)(t)| \le c \sup_f L(F_{n,f}, F_f)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 8
nodes.statement: WLOG $\mathcal{F}$ centered. (i) $\Rightarrow$ (ii): $GC(P)$ implies $P$-integrable envelope and $\mathcal{F}_M \in GC(P)$ for all $M$, then apply Theorem 7. (ii) $\Rightarrow$ (i): $L(F_{n,f_M}, F_{f_M}) \le L(F_{n,f}, F_f)$ plus Theorem 7 plus standard truncation.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 9
nodes.statement: Choose $M$ with $\mathcal{F}_M = \mathcal{F}$. $BCLT(P)$ gives $\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum \varepsilon_i\delta_{X_i}\|_\mathcal{F} = O(n^{-1/2})$, so Theorem 10 implies $O_P(n^{-1/4})$. For the entropy-bound case, refine the proof of Theorem 10 using subgaussian entropy estimates: $\mathbb{E}_\varepsilon \hat R_n(\tilde G_\delta) \le c/\sqrt{n\delta^\alpha}$, optimize $\delta = c/n^{1/(2+\alpha)}$, then Borel–Cantelli.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 11
nodes.statement: Decompose $\mathbb{E}\sup_{\tilde f}n^{-1}\sum \varepsilon_j m_f(X_j, Y_j)$ via $I_{Y_j = y}$ indicators. Use that $\{\varepsilon_j(2I_{Y_j=y}-1)\}$ is i.i.d. Rademacher to symmetrize, then apply Lemma 2 to bound the maximum class by factor $2(M-1)$, finally invoke Theorem 2 with continuous step approximation $\varphi$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 12
nodes.statement: $R_n(\mathrm{conv}(H)) = \mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum \varepsilon_i\delta_{X_i}\|_{\mathrm{conv}(H)} = \mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum \varepsilon_i\delta_{X_i}\|_H = R_n(H)$ since the Rademacher process is linear. Then apply Theorem 2.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 13
nodes.statement: Apply Theorem 2 to $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{H}_l$, then prove the inductive Gaussian-complexity bound $G_n(\mathcal{H}_l) \le \prod_{j=1}^l (2L_jA_j+1)\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum g_i\delta_{X_i}\|_H$. Use $G_n(\mathcal{H}_l) \le G_n(\mathcal{G}_l) + G_n(\mathcal{H}_{l-1})$, Slepian's Lemma applied to processes $Z_1(f) = n^{-1/2}\sum g_i\sigma_l(f(X_i))$ vs $Z_2(f) = L_l n^{-1/2}\sum g_i f(X_i)$, plus $G_n(\mathcal{G}_l) = A_l G_n(\mathcal{H}_{l-1})$ via symmetric convex hull.

nodes.name: Apply Theorem 2 to $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{H}_l$
nodes.statement: Theorem 2 (Gaussian version) applied to $\mathcal{F} = \mathcal{H}_l(A_1,\dots,A_l)$ gives the bound with $G_n(\mathcal{H}_l)$ in place of the product factor. Need to bound $G_n(\mathcal{H}_l)$.

nodes.name: Decompose $G_n(\mathcal{H}_l) \le G_n(\mathcal{G}_l) + G_n(\mathcal{H}_{l-1})$
nodes.statement: Since $\mathcal{H}_l = \mathcal{G}_l \cup \mathcal{H}_{l-1}$ where $\mathcal{G}_l$ is the new layer-$l$ neurons, $\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum g_i\delta_{X_i}\|_{\mathcal{H}_l} \le \mathbb{E}\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{G}_l} + \mathbb{E}\|\cdot\|_{\mathcal{H}_{l-1}}$.

nodes.name: Slepian comparison removes sigmoid
nodes.statement: For $Z_1(f) = n^{-1/2}\sum g_i \sigma_l(f(X_i))$, $Z_2(f) = L_l n^{-1/2}\sum g_i f(X_i)$: increments inequality $\mathbb{E}|Z_1(f)-Z_1(h)|^2 \le L_l^2 n^{-1}\sum |f(X_i)-h(X_i)|^2 = \mathbb{E}|Z_2(f)-Z_2(h)|^2$ via Lipschitz of $\sigma_l$. Slepian's Lemma gives $\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum g_i\delta_{X_i}\|_{\mathcal{G}_l} \le 2L_l \mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum g_i\delta_{X_i}\|_{G_l'}$.

nodes.name: Symmetric convex hull and induction
nodes.statement: $G_l' = A_l \mathrm{conv}_s(\mathcal{H}_{l-1})$ gives $\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum g_i\delta_{X_i}\|_{G_l'} = A_l \mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum g_i\delta_{X_i}\|_{\mathcal{H}_{l-1}}$. Combining with the decomposition: $G_n(\mathcal{H}_l) \le (2L_l A_l + 1)G_n(\mathcal{H}_{l-1})$. Iterate by induction on $l$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 14
nodes.statement: Decompose over network depths $\ell(f) = l$ and dyadic shells $W_j(f) \in [2^{k_j-1}, 2^{k_j})$. For each fixed $(l, k_1, \dots, k_l)$, apply Theorem 13 with $A_j = 2^{k_j}$. Sum the resulting tail bounds: $\sum_l \sum_{k_j \in \mathbb{Z}\setminus\{0\}} 2 \exp(-\sum_j \alpha\log(|k_j|+1) - 2t^2) = 2(3 - 2\zeta(\alpha))^{-1}\exp(-2t^2)$.

nodes.name: Proof of Theorem 15
nodes.statement: First bound is direct from Theorem 14 plus the definition of $\tilde f_S$ as penalized minimizer. Second bound: prove $P\{\exists f \in F\,\exists\delta\,P_n\{\tilde f \le \delta\} > P\{\tilde f \le 2\delta\} + (2\sqrt{2\pi}/\delta)G(f)G_n(H) + \dots\} \le 2(3-2\zeta(\alpha))^{-1}e^{-2t^2}$, then combine with the first bound and contradiction-style implication.

nodes.name: AdaBoost
nodes.statement: Iterative voting algorithm that, after $N$ rounds with weak learner returning $h_k \in H$, outputs the convex combination $f_S(x) := (\sum_{k=1}^N \alpha_k h_k(x))/\sum_k \alpha_k$.
nodes.pseudocode:
Initialize $w_j^{(1)} = n^{-1}$.
For $k = 1, \dots, N$:
  Call weak learner with weights $w^{(k)}$ to get $h_k \in H$.
  Compute $e_k := P_{n, w^{(k)}}\{y \ne h_k\}$.
  Set $\alpha_k := \tfrac{1}{2}\log((1-e_k)/e_k)$.
  Update $w_j^{(k+1)} := w_j^{(k)}\exp(-Y_j\alpha_k h_k(X_j))/Z_k$ where $Z_k = \sum_j w_j^{(k)}\exp(-Y_j\alpha_k h_k(X_j))$.
Return $f_S(x) = (\sum_k \alpha_k h_k(x))/\sum_k \alpha_k$.

nodes.name: Boosting loop over rounds
nodes.statement: For $k = 1, \dots, N$: invoke weak learner to obtain $h_k$ with weighted error $e_k = P_{n, w^{(k)}}\{y \ne h_k\}$, set $\alpha_k = \tfrac{1}{2}\log((1-e_k)/e_k)$, update weights $w_j^{(k+1)} = w_j^{(k)}\exp(-Y_j\alpha_k h_k(X_j))/Z_k$.

nodes.name: Output combined classifier
nodes.statement: Return $f_S(x) := (\sum_{k=1}^N \alpha_k h_k(x))/\sum_{k=1}^N \alpha_k$.

nodes.name: AdaBoost margin bound application
nodes.statement: Choosing decreasing $\varphi$ with $\varphi(u) \le e^{-u}$ and $\delta = 1/\sum_k \alpha_k \wedge 1$ in Theorem 12 yields, with probability $\ge 1-\alpha$: $P\{\tilde f_S \le 0\} \le \sum_{k=1}^N 2\sqrt{e_k(1-e_k)} + 8(\log\sum_k(1-e_k)/e_k \vee 1)R_n(H) + ((\log\log_2(\dots))/n)^{1/2} + ((\log(2/\alpha))/(2n))^{1/2}$.

nodes.name: Counterexample for sharpness of $1/\delta$ factor
nodes.statement: Sequence $X_n = (\varepsilon_{kn}(2\log(k+1))^{-1/2})_{k\ge 1}$ in $\ell^\infty$ with $\mathcal{F}$ canonical projections; used in Proposition 1 to show that $1/\delta$ in Theorem 2 cannot be replaced by $1/\phi(\delta)$ when $\phi(\delta)/\delta \to \infty$.

nodes.name: Optimality example for Lévy convergence rates
nodes.statement: Sequence $X_n = (\varepsilon_{kn}(2\log(k+1))^{-1/2-\beta})_{k\ge 1}$ with $\beta = 1/\alpha - 1/2$ for $\alpha \in (0,2]$; entropy condition $H_{d_{P_n,2}}(\mathcal{F};u) \le D u^{-\alpha}$ holds and the rate $n^{-1/(2+\alpha)}$ is achieved with matching lower bound (Proposition 2).

nodes.name: Constant tightening in Theorem 2
nodes.statement: The constant $8$ in front of the Rademacher complexity and $2\sqrt{2\pi}$ in front of the Gaussian complexity can be replaced by $4c$ and $\sqrt{2\pi}c$, respectively, for any $c > 1$, with minor changes in the logarithmic term.

nodes.name: Improved factors for special architectures
nodes.statement: For multilayer perceptrons (each layer linked only to the previous), $\prod_j(2L_jA_j+1)$ in Theorem 13 can be replaced by $\prod_j 2L_j A_j$. For odd sigmoids in general feedforward architecture, the factor becomes $\prod_j(L_j A_j+1)$; for multilayer perceptrons with odd sigmoids, $\prod_j L_j A_j$.

nodes.name: $GC(P)$ does not imply uniform Lévy + indicator class GC
nodes.statement: $\mathcal{F} \in GC(P)$ does not imply $\sup_f \sup_t |F_{n,f}(t) - F_f(t)| \to 0$ a.s. Counterexample: unit ball in dual of infinite-dimensional separable Banach space, where the class of halfspaces is not $GC(P)$ (Sazonov 1963).

nodes.name: Bartlett-style margin bound (Section 1 schematic)
nodes.statement: $\inf_{\delta > 0}\big[n^{-1}\sum_{j=1}^n I_{\{Y_j\hat g(X_j) \le \delta\}} + C(G)\varphi(\delta) C(H)/\sqrt{n}\big]$

nodes.name: Improved $\gamma$-bound
nodes.statement: $\mathrm{generr}(g) \le C_\gamma / (n^{1-\gamma/2}\hat\delta_n(\gamma;g)^\gamma)$

nodes.name: Convex hull entropy bound for VC class
nodes.statement: $H_{d_{P_n,2}}(\mathrm{conv}(H);u) \le \sup_{Q \in P(S)} H_{d_{Q,2}}(\mathrm{conv}(H);u) \le D u^{-2(V-1)/V}$ where $V = V(H)$ is VC-dimension.
nodes.origin_citation: Dudley; Ball–Pajor; van der Vaart–Wellner; Carl; Haussler

nodes.name: Talagrand concentration inequalities for empirical processes
nodes.statement: Concentration of $\|P_n - P\|_{\mathcal{F}}$ around its mean for bounded function classes, with subgaussian-type tails depending on the variance and supremum.

nodes.name: Slepian's Lemma
nodes.statement: If $\{Z_1(t)\}, \{Z_2(t)\}$ are centered Gaussian processes with $\mathbb{E}|Z_1(s) - Z_1(t)|^2 \le \mathbb{E}|Z_2(s) - Z_2(t)|^2$ for all $s,t$, then $\mathbb{E}\sup_t Z_1(t) \le \mathbb{E}\sup_t Z_2(t)$.

nodes.name: Rademacher comparison inequality
nodes.statement: If $\varphi : \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is a contraction with $\varphi(0) = 0$, then $\mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum \varepsilon_i \varphi(f(X_i))\|_{\mathcal{F}} \le 2 L(\varphi) \mathbb{E}\|n^{-1}\sum \varepsilon_i f(X_i)\|_{\mathcal{F}}$.
